skill.name: global-commenting
skill.description: Guides concise, lasting code comments that explain complex logic, business rules, and documentation blocks without repeating obvious behavior.
skill.summary: Write focused code comments that explain intent and keep source files maintainable.
skill.author: DevanB

security_audit.summary: The static path traversal finding is confirmed because SKILL.md directs the agent to read a Markdown file outside the skill directory. No evidence found of prompt injection, network access, external command execution, or environment variable access.

remediation.suggestion: Move the referenced commenting standard into the skill package or inline the required guidance in SKILL.md.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 26 links to ../../../agent-os/standards/global/commenting.md and instructs the agent to use that file for details. This traverses outside the skill directory and can cause unintended filesystem reads or missing external dependencies.

high_findings.title: Path traversal sequence
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: SKILL.md line 26 links to ../../../agent-os/standards/global/commenting.md and instructs the agent to use that file for details. This traverses outside the skill directory and can cause unintended filesystem reads or missing external dependencies.

content.value_statement: Unclear or stale comments make code harder to maintain. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to write focused comments that explain intent.
actual_capabilities: Guides comment writing for PHP, TypeScript, JavaScript, and other code files.
Helps decide when to comment and when to refactor for clearer code.
Supports PHPDoc blocks for classes, methods, functions, and complex array shapes.
Supports JSDoc and TSDoc guidance for TypeScript and JavaScript functions.
Reviews existing comments for relevance, permanence, and necessity.
Encourages comments that explain non-obvious business logic and algorithm choices.
limitations: Does not execute linters, formatters, or documentation generators.
Requires access to the target source files for specific recommendations.
Full guidance depends on a referenced standard outside the packaged skill.
Does not replace project-specific documentation rules or reviewer judgment.

use_cases.title: Review Comments Before Merge
use_cases.description: Check whether comments explain durable intent and remove notes that only repeat the code.

use_cases.title: Add PHP Documentation Blocks
use_cases.description: Create practical PHPDoc for classes, methods, functions, and complex data shapes.

use_cases.title: Clarify Complex Frontend Logic
use_cases.description: Add concise JSDoc or TSDoc where TypeScript or JavaScript behavior is not obvious.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Comments
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this file for comments that are outdated, obvious, or too temporary. Suggest only comments that explain durable intent.

prompt_templates.title: Add Minimal Documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Add the minimum useful documentation for this function. Explain non-obvious inputs, outputs, and business rules without repeating the code.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Before Commenting
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve clarity in a confusing section
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this confusing code path. First suggest naming or structure changes, then add comments only where clarity still requires them.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Project Comment Standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these related files for comment quality. Identify inconsistent PHPDoc, JSDoc, TSDoc, and stale comments, then recommend a consistent standard.

output_examples.input: A PHP service method has several comments that restate each assignment and one complex pricing exception.
output_examples.output: The output keeps one comment explaining the pricing exception and removes comments that repeat obvious assignments.

output_examples.input: A TypeScript helper has unclear date handling and no documentation for an edge case.
output_examples.output: The output adds a short TSDoc note for the edge case and recommends clearer names for the date variables.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks whether a new comment about a recent bug fix should remain.
output_examples.output: The output recommends replacing temporary history with a durable explanation of the invariant that the code must preserve.

best_practices: Explain why complex logic exists, not what each simple statement does.
Prefer clear names and structure before adding explanatory comments.
Keep documentation evergreen by avoiding temporary history and release notes.
anti_patterns: Do not add comments that restate obvious code behavior.
Do not document short-term fixes as permanent source comments.
Do not use comments to hide unclear naming or confusing structure.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps write concise code comments and documentation blocks that explain non-obvious intent.

faq.question: Which languages does it mention?
faq.answer: It mentions PHP, TypeScript, JavaScript, PHPDoc, JSDoc, and TSDoc.

faq.question: Can it remove comments?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify outdated, obvious, or temporary comments that should be removed.

faq.question: Does it generate documentation sites?
faq.answer: No. It provides writing guidance but does not run documentation generators.

faq.question: Is it useful during code review?
faq.answer: Yes. Reviewers can use it to check comment quality before merging changes.

faq.question: Does it prefer comments or self-documenting code?
faq.answer: It prefers clear code first, then comments for intent that remains non-obvious.
